G5100.def:
τις, neut., τι, genitive, τινός, 
enclitic indefinite pron., related to interrog. τίς as πού, πως, ποτέ to ποῦ, πῶς, πότε. 
__I. As subst., 
__1. one, a certain one: Luc 9:49, Jean 11:1, Actes 5:25, al.; pl., τίνες, certain, some: Luc 13:1, Actes 15:1, Romains 3:8, al. 
__2. someone, anyone, something, anything: Matthieu 12:29, Marc 9:30, Luc 8:46, Jean 2:25, Actes 17:25, Romains 5:7, al.; = indef., one (French on), Marc 8:4, Jean 2:25, Romains 8:24, al.; pl., τινες, some, Marc 14:4, al. 
__II. II. As adj., 
__1. a certain: Matthieu 18:12, Luc 1:5 8:27, Actes 3:2, al.; with proper names, Marc 15:21, Luc 23:26, al.; with genitive partit., Luc 7:19, al. 
__2. some: Mrk.16:[8], Jean 5:14, Actes 17:21 24:24, Hébreux 11:40, al.

G5101.def:
τίς, neut., τί, genitive, τίνος, interrog. pron., [in LXX for מָה ,מִי ;] in masc. and fem., 
who, which, what?; in neut., which, what?, used both in direct and in indirect questions. 
__I. I. As subst., 
__1. 1. masc., fem.: τίς; who, what?, Matthieu 3:7 26:68; Marc 11:28, Luc 9:9, al. mult.; with genitive partit., Actes 7:52, Hébreux 1:5, al; before ἐκ (= genitive partit.), Matthieu 6:27, Luc 14:28, Jean 8:46; = ποῖος, Marc 4:41 6:2, Luc 19:3, Actes 17:19, al.; = πότερος (M, Pr., 77), Matthieu 21:31 27:17, Luc 22:27, al.; = ὅς or ὅστις (rare in cl.; cf. Bl., §50, 5; M, Pr., 93), Actes 13:25. 
__2. Neut.: τί; what?, Matthieu 5:47 11:7, Marc 10:3, al.; χάριν τίνος, 1 Jean 3:12; διὰ τί, Matthieu 9:11, al.; εἰς τί, Matthieu 14:31, al.; elliptically, ἵνα τί (sc. γένηται), why, Matthieu 9:5, al.; τί οὖν, Romains 3:9 6:1, 15 1 Corinthiens 14:15, al.; τί γάρ, Romains 3:3, Phi 1:18; τί ἐμοὶ (ὑμῖν) καὶ σοί, see: ἔγω. 
__II. As adj.: who? what? which?, Matthieu 5:46, Luc 14:31, Jean 2:18, al. 
__III. As adv.: = διὰ τι (τί ὅτι), why, Matthieu 6:28, Marc 4:40, Luc 6:46, Jean 18:23, al.; in rhet. questions, = a negation, Matthieu 27:4, Jean 21:22, 23 1 Corinthiens 5:12 7:16, al. in exclamations (like Heb. מָה), how (2 Rois 6:20, Psaumes 3:2, al.), Luc 12:49.

G5102.def:
τίτλος, -ου, ὁ 
(Lat. titulus), [in Aq., Sm., Th.: Jérémie 21:4 * ;] 
a title, inscription: Jean 19:19-20 (in Christian Inscr., epitaph, see MM. xxiv).†

G5103.def:
Τίτος, -ου, ὁ 
Titus; 
__1. St. Paul's disciple and companion: 2 Corinthiens 2:13 7:6 7:13-14 8:6 8:16 8:23 12:18, Galates 2:1, 3, 2 Timothée 4:10, Tite 1:4, subscr., Rec. (Τῖτος). 
__2. One surnamed Justus: Actes 18:7, RV (T, WH, Τίτιος).†

G5105.def:
τοι-γαρ-οῦν 
an inferential particle, [in LXX: Job 22:10 24:22, Sir.41:16, al. ;] 
wherefore then, so therefore: 1 Thessaloniciens 4:8, Hébreux 12:1 (Hat., Plat., al.).†

G5106.def:
τοί-νυν 
an inferential particle, [in LXX: Ésaïe 3:10 5:13 27:4, Wis.1:11 8:9, a1. * ;] 
accordingly, therefore: as in cl., after the first word in a sentence, 1 Corinthiens 9:26; accusative to later usage, at the beginning, Luc 20:25, Hébreux 13:13.†

G5107.def: antecedent to οἷος, as ἀοιδοῦ τοιοῦδ᾽ οἷος ὅδ᾽ ἐστί of such a minstrel as is this one, (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, ἀλλ᾽ ὅδ᾽ ἐγὼ τοιόσδε here am I such as you see , (Odyssey by Homer):—;also, so great, so noble, so bad , τοιάδε λαίφη such clothes, i. e. so bad , (Odyssey by Homer); τοσόσδε καὶ τοιόσδε (Herdotus Historicus):—;also with a qualifying word, τοιόσδ᾽ ἠμὲν δέμας ἠδὲ καὶ ἔργα such both in form and works, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with the Art., ὁ τ. ἀνήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; οἱ τοιοίδε (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐν τῷ τοιῷδε in such circumstances, (Herdotus Historicus):—;the sense is made more indefinite in τοιόσδε τις such a one, (Thucydides):—;neuter plural τοιάδε as follows , τοιαῦτα as aforesaid , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G5108.def:
τοιοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
(as usually in Att.. prose. Ep. and Ion. neut. -οῦτον in Al., Actes 21:25, Rec. only), 
correlat. of οἷος, ὁποῖος, ὥς, etc., 
such as this, of such a kind, such: Matthieu 9:8 18:5, Marc 4:33 6:2 7:13 9:37 (T, τούτων), Jean 9:16, Actes 16:24, 1 Corinthiens 5:1 11:16, 2 Corinthiens 3:4 3:12 12:3, Hébreux 7:26 8:1 12:3 13:16, Jacques 4:16; οἷος . . . τ., 1 Corinthiens 15:48, 2 Corinthiens 10:11; id. pleonast. (see Bl., § 50, 4), Marc 13:19; before ὁποῖος, Actes 26:29; ὥς, Phm 9. As subst., anarth: pl., Luc 9:9; with art., ὁ τ., such a one (Bl., § 47, 9; Ellic. on Galates 5:21): Actes 22:22, 1 Corinthiens 5:5, al.; pl., Matthieu 19:14, Marc 10:14, al.; neut. pl., Actes 19:25, Romains 1:32, al

G5109.def:
τοῖχος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for קִיר ;] 
a wall, esp. of a house: figuratively, Actes 23:3 (cf. τεῖχος).†

G5110.def:
τόκος, -ου, ὁ
(τίκτω), [in LXX for נֶשֶׁךְ, etc. ;] 
__(a) a bringing forth, birth; 
__(b) offspring. Metaphorical, of the produce of money lent out, interest, usury (cf. Merch. of Venice, I, iii, "a breed of barren metal "): Matthieu 25:27, Luc 19:23 (Soph., Plat., al.).†

G5111.def:
τολμάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Job 15:12 (לָקַח), Esther 1:18 7:5 (לֵב מָלֵא) Jdth.14:13, 2Ma.4:2, 3Ma.3:21 R, 4Ma.8:18 * ;] 
to have courage, to venture, dare, be bold: absol, 2 Corinthiens 11:21; before ἐπί, 2 Corinthiens 10:2; with inf. (Bl., § 69, 4), Matthieu 22:46, Marc 12:34, Luc 20:40, Jean 21:12, Actes 5:13 7:32, Romains 15:18, 1 Corinthiens 6:1, 2 Corinthiens 10:12, Philippiens 1:14, Ju 9; to submit to (in cl. usually absol. in this sense), Romains 5:7 (see Field, Notes, 155); τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν, took courage and went in (see Field, op. cit., 44), Marc 15:43 (cf. ἀπο-τολμάω).†

G5112.def:
τολμηρῶς 
adv., (τολμηρός, bold, daring), 
boldly: compar., -ότερως (T, Rec. -ότερον), Romains 15:15.†

G5113.def:
τολμητής, -οῦ, ὁ 
(τολμάω), 
a bold, daring man: 2 Pierre 2:10 (Thuc.).†

G5115.def:
τόξον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for קֶשֶׁת ;] 
a bow: Apocalypse 6:2.†

G5116.def:
τοπάζιον, -ου, τό
(and τόπαζος, ὁ), [in LXX: Exode 28:17 35:17 (Exode 39:10), Job 28:19, Eze.28:13 (פִּטְדָה), Psaumes 119:127 (פָּז)* ;] 
topaz: Apocalypse 21:20 (see Swete, in l).†

G5117.def:
τόπος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for מָקוֹם ;] 
place: Luc 4:37 10:1, 32 Jean 5:13 6:10, Actes 12:17, 1 Corinthiens 1:2, al.; τ. ἅγιος (cf. Ésaïe 60:13), Matthieu 24:15; ἔρημος, Matthieu 14:13, al.; πεδινός, Luc 6:17; ἄνυδρος (pl.), Matthieu 12:43, Luc 11:24; κατὰ τόπος (BV, in divers places), Matthieu 24:7, Marc 13:8; τραχεῖς τ., Actes 27:29; τ. διθάλασσος (which see), ib. 41; ἑτοιμάζειν τ., Jean 14:2, 3; ἔχειν, Apocalypse 12:6; διδόναι, Luc 14:9; with genitive defin., τ. βασάνου, Luc 16:28; τ. καταπαύσεως, Actes 7:49; κρανίου, Matthieu 27:33, Marc 15:22, Jean 19:17; before οὗ, Romains 9:26; ὅπου, Matthieu 28:6, Marc 16:6, Jean 4:20 6:23 10:40 11:30 19:41; ἐν ᾧ, Jean 11:6; ἐφ ̓ ᾧ, Actes 7:33; of a place which a person or thing occupies, Apocalypse 2:5 6:14 12:8; τ. μαχαίρας, Matthieu 26:52; ὁ ἴδιος τ., Actes 1:25; of a place in a book, Luc 4:17 (cf. Clem. Rom., I Co., 8, 4). Metaphorical, of condition, station, occasion, opportunity or power: Actes 25:16, Romains 12:19 15:23, Éphésiens 4:27 (cf. Sir.38:12). 
SYN.: χώρα (extensive), region; χωρίον (enclosed), a piece of ground. τ. is "a portion of space viewed in reference to its occupancy, or as appropriated to a thing " (Grimm-Thayer, see word).

G5118.def:
τοσοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
(Hébreux 7:22) and (elsewhere, as usually in Attic) -οῦτον, correlat. of ὅσος, of quantity, size, number, so great, so much, pl., so many: Matthieu 8:10 Luc 7:9, Hébreux 12:1, Apocalypse 18:7, 16; of time, so long, χρόνος, Jean 14:9, Hébreux 4:7; pl., Luc 15:29 (ἔτη), Jean 12:37 21:11, 1 Corinthiens 14:10; before ὥστε, Matthieu 15:33; absol.: pl., Jean 6:9, Galates 3:4; of price, τοσούτου, Actes 5:8; dative, τοσούτῳ κρείττων, Hébreux 1:4; τ. μᾶλλον ὅσῳ, Hébreux 10:25; καθ᾽ ὅσον . . . κατὰ τ., Hébreux 7:22.†

G5121.def:
τοὐναντίον 
by crasis for τὸ ἐνανίον, neut. accusative, used adverbially, on the contrary, contrariwise: 2 Corinthiens 2:7, Galates 2:7, 1 Pierre 3:9.†

G5122.def:
τοὔνομα 
by crasis for τὸ ὄνομα, accusative absol., 
by name: Matthieu 27:57.†

G5131.def:
τράγος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for עַתּוּד, also for צָפִיר, תַּיִשׁ ;] 
a he-goat: Hébreux 9:12-13, 19 10:4.†

G5132.def:
τράπεζα, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for שֻׁלְחָן, also for לֶחֶם, etc. ;] 
__1. a table, dining-table: Matthieu 15:27, Marc 7:28, Luc 16:21 19:23 22:21, 30; of the table of shewbread, Hébreux 9:2. By meton., of food provided (see DB, iv, 670 a): Actes 16:34, Romains 11:9" (LXX) 1 Corinthiens 10:21; διακονεῖν ταῖς τ., Actes 6:2 (cf. Page, in l, but see infr.). 
__2. A money-changer's table, a bank (Dem., Arist., al.): Matthieu 21:12, Marc 11:15, Luc 19:23, Jean 2:15; so also accusative to Dr. Field (Notes, 113), Actes 6:2 (but see supr.).†

G5133.def:
τραπεζείτης (Rec. -ζίτης, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ 
(τράπεζα), 
a money­changer, banker: Matthieu 25:27 (Dem., Plut., al.).†

G5134.def:
τραῦμα, -τος, τό 
[in LXX for פָּצַע, חָלַל, etc. ;] 
a wowed: Luc 10:34.†

G5135.def:
τραυματίζω
(τραῦμα), [in LXX chiefly for חָלַל ;] 
to wound: Luc 20:12, Actes 19:16.†

G5136.def:
τραχηλίζω
(τράχηλος), 
prop., of wrestlers, 
to take by the throat, hence (Philo), to prostrate, overthrow. Metaphorical, but in what sense and from what age it is doubtful (see Westc., Rendall, on He, l.with; DB, iii, 625n), τραχηλισμένα, laid open (RV, Westc.; downcast, Rendall): Hébreux 4:13.†

G5137.def:
τράχηλος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for צַוַּאר, also forעֹרֶף, etc. ;] 
the neck: Matthieu 18:6, Marc 9:42, Luc 17:2; ἐπιπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὸν τ., to embrace (Genèse 46:29), Luc 15:20, Actes 20:37. Metaphorical, ὑποθεῖναι τὸν ἑαυτοῦ τ. (for similar phrase in π., see Zorell, see word), Romains 16:4; ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τ., Actes 15:10.†

G5138.def:
τραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 40:4 (רֶכֶס), etc. ;] 
rough: ὁδοί (Is, l.with), Luc 3:5 (LXX); τοποί (i.e. rocky), Actes 27:29.†

G5139.def:
Τραχωνῖτις, -ιδος, ἡ
(τραχύς) 
Trachonitis, a rough region S. of Damascus (in FlJ, sometimes ἡ Τ., sometimes ό Τράχων): ἡ Τ. χώρα, Luc 3:1.†

G5140.def:
τρεῖς, οἱ, αἱ, τρία, τά
three: Matthieu 12:40, al.; μετὰ τ. ἡμέρας = τῇ τρίτῃ ἡ., Marc 10:34, al. (cf. Field, Notes, 11 ff.) 
Τρεῖς Ταβέρναι 
(see: ταβέρνη), 
Three Taverns (Lit. Tres Tabernae) a halting place on the Appian Way: Actes 28:15 (see DB, iv, 690).†

G5141.def:
τρέμω 
to tremble, esp. with fear: Marc 5:33, Luc 8:47; with ptcp. (in cl more frequently with inf.), 2 Pierre 2:10.†

G5142.def:
τρέφω 
[in LXX for חָיָה hi., גָּדַל pi., אָכַל hi., etc. ;] 
__1. to make to grow, bring up, rear (cl.; 1Ma.3:33 1Mac 11:39): Luc 4:16 (T, WH, mg., ἀνατ-) 
__2. to nourish, feed: Matthieu 6:26 25:37, Luc 12:24, Actes 12:20, Apocalypse 12:6, 14; of a mother, to give suck, Luc 23:29; of animals, to fatten (Jérémie 26:21 (Jérémie 46:21), figuratively, Jacques 5:5 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐκ-, ἐν-τρέφω).†

G5143.def:
τρέχω 
[in LXX chiefly for רוּץ ;] 
to run: Marc 5:6, Jean 20:2, 4, 1 Corinthiens 9:24 9:26; with inf., Matthieu 28:8; before ἐπί, Luc 24:12 [T [WH] R, mg., om.]; εἰς, Apocalypse 9:9; ptcp., δραμών, with indic., Matthieu 27:48, Marc 15:36, Luc 15:20. Metaphorical, from runners in a race, of swiftness or of effort to attain an end: Romains 9:16, Galates 2:2 5:7, Philippiens 2:16; τ. ἀγῶνα (Hdt., Eur., al.), Hébreux 12:1; ὁ λόγος τ. κυρίου (cf. Psaumes 147:4), ἕως τάχους δραμεῖται ὁ λ. αὐτοῦ), 2 Thessaloniciens 3:1 (cf. εἰς-, κατα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ἐπι-συν-, ὑπο-τρέχω) 
δράμω, obsol., to run, see: τρέχω

G5144.def:
τριάκοντα, ἱο, αἱ, τά indecl. 
(τρεῖς), 
thirty: Matthieu 13:8, al.

G5146.def:
τρίβολος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Genèse 3:18, Osée 10:8 (דַּרְדַּר), 2 Rois 12:31 (חָרִיץ), Proverbes 22:5 (צֵן)* ;] 
a thistle: Matthieu 7:16, Hébreux 6:8.†

G5147.def:
τρίβος, -ου, -ἡ
(τρίβω), [in LXX for מְסִלָּה, נָתִיב, etc. ;] 
a beaten track, a path: Matthieu 3:3, Marc 1:3, Luc 3:4" (LXX) .†

G5148.def:
τριετία, -ας, ἡ
(τρεῖς, ἔτος), 
a period of three years: Actes 20:31.†

G5149.def:
τρίζω 
[in Aq.: Amos 2:13; Sm.: Ésaïe 38:14 * ;] 
__1. prop., of sounds by animals, to cry, chirp, etc. 
__2. Of other sounds, e.g., trans., τ. ὀδόντας, to gnash or grind the teeth: Marc 9:18.†

G5150.def:
τρίμηνος, -ον
(τρεῖς, μήν) [in LXX (neut.): Genèse 38:24, 4Ki.23:31 B 4Ki.24:8, 2 Chroniques 36:2 36:9 (חֹדֶשׁ שָׁלוֹשׁ) * ;] 
of three months; as subst., τὸ τ. (= cl. ἡ τ.), a space of three months (Polyb., al.; LXX): Hébreux 11:23.†

G5151.def:
τρίς
(τρεῖς), 
adv., 
thrice: Matthieu 26:34, 75, Marc 14:30, 72 Luc 22:34, 61 Jean 13:38, 2 Corinthiens 11:25 12:8; ἐπὶ τ., Actes 10:16 11:10.†

G5152.def:
τρίστεγος, -ον (τρεῖς, στέγη) 
[in Sm.: Genèse 6:17(16), Eze.42:6 * ;] 
of three stories: τὸ τ. (sc. ὄκημα), 
the third story, Actes 20:9 (Dion., FlJ, al.).†

G5154.def:
τρίτος, -η, -ον 
the third: Matthieu 22:26, Marc 12:21 15:25, Luc 24:21, Actes 2:15, al.; τῇ τ. ἡμέρᾳ (i.e. the next day but one: Xen., al.; see Field, Notes, 11 ff.), Matthieu 16:21, Luc 24:46, al.; substantively, accusative masc., τρίτον, a third (servant), Luc 20:12; neut., τὸ τ., with genitive, the third part of: Apocalypse 8:7-12 9:15, 18 12:4. As adv., τὸ τ., the third time: Marc 14:41, Jean 21:17; anarth., τρίτον, a third time, Luc 23:22, Jean 21:14, 2 Corinthiens 12:14 13:1; in enumerations, thirdly, 1 Corinthiens 12:28; ἐκ τ., a third time, Matthieu 26:44

G5155.def:
τρίχινος, -η, -ον
(θρίξ), [in LXX: Zacharie 13:4 (שֵׂעָר), Exode 26:7 * ;] 
of hair: στόκος, Apocalypse 6:12 (Xen., Plat., al.).†

G5156.def:
τρόμος, -ου, ὁ
(τρέμω), [in LXX for רַעַד, רַעַד, פַּחַד, etc. ;] 
trembling, quaking, esp. from fear: Marc 16:8; φόβος κ. τ. (as in Genèse 9:2, Exode 15:16, Deutéronome 2:25, Ésaïe 19:16, al.), 1 Corinthiens 2:3, 2 Corinthiens 7:15, Éphésiens 6:5, Philippiens 2:12.†

G5157.def:
τροπή, -ῆς, ἡ
(τρέπω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 33:14, Job 38:33, Wis.7:18, al. ;] 
a turning: esp. of the revolution of heavenly bodies, figuratively, Jacques 1:17 (see: ἀποσκίασμα).†

G5158.def:
τρόπος, -ου, ὁ
(τρέπω), [in LXX chiefly (ὃν τ.) for אֲשֶׁר ;] 
__1. a way, manner, fashion: Matthieu 23:37, Luc 13:34, Actes 1:11 7:28, 2 Timothée 3:8, Ju 7; καθ᾽ ὃν τ., Actes 15:11 27:25 (ef. MM, xxv); κατὰ πάντα τ., Romains 3:2; κατὰ μηδένα τ. (4Ma.4:24, al.), 2 Thessaloniciens 2:3; (ἐν) παντὶ τ., Philippiens 1:18, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:16 
__2. Of persons, manner of life, character (Hdt., Æsch., al.): Hébreux 13:5.†

G5159.def:
τροπο-φορέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 1:31 B.l (נָשָׂא) * ;] 
__1. to bear another's manners (R, txt., suffered he their manners): with accusative of person(s), Actes 13:18 (Rec., WH, R, txt.; ἐτροφο-, T, R, mg.). 
__2. = τροφοφορέω (which see), (see Kühner3, I, 276): Ac, l.with†

G5160.def:
τροφή, -ῆς, ἡ
(τρέφω), [in LXX for לֶחֶם, מָזוֹן, אֹכֶל, etc. ;] 
nourishment, food: Matthieu 3:4 6:25 10:10 24:45, Luc 12:23, Jean 4:8, Actes 2:46 9:19 14:17 27:33-34, 36 27:38 Jacques 2:15. Metaphorical: Hébreux 5:12, 14.†

G5162.def:
τροφός, -oῦ, ἡ
(τρέφω), [in LXX: Genèse 35:8, 4Ki.11:2, 2 Chroniques 22:11 Ésaïe 49:23 (יָנַק) * ;] 
a nurse: 1 Thessaloniciens 2:7.†

G5163.def:
τροχιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(τροχός), [in LXX: Proverbes 2:15 4:11, 26-27 5:6, 21 (מַעְגָּל), Eze.27:19 A* ;] 
the track of a wheel, hence, a track, path: figuratively, Hébreux 12:13 (LXX) †

G5164.def:
τροχός, -οῦ, τό
(τρέχω), [in LXX chiefly for אוֹפָן ;] 
a wheel: Jacques 3:6 (see Mayor, Hort, in l).†

G5165.def:
τρύβλιον (Rec. τρυβλίον), -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for קְעָרָה ;] 
a bowl, dish: Matthieu 26:23, Marc 14:20 (Hippocr., Aristoph., Pint., al.).†

G5166.def:
τρυγάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX for קָצַר, בָּצַר, etc. ;] 
to gather in: with accusative, 
__(a) of the fruit, Luc 6:44, Apocalypse 14:18; 
__(b) of that from which it is gathered, Apocalypse 14:19.†

G5167.def:
τρυγών, -όνος, ἡ
(τρύζω, to murmur, coo), [in LXX for תּוֹר ;] 
a turtle-dove: Luc 2:24.†

G5168.def:
τρυμαλιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(τρύω, to wear away), [in LXX: Jérémie 13:4 (נָקִיק), etc. ;] 
= τρύμη, a hole: τ. ῥαφίδος, eye of a needle, Marc 10:25.†
SYN.: τρῆμα, τρύπημα

G5169.def:
τρύπημα, -τος, τό
(τρυπάω, to bore) 
a hole: τ. ῥαφιδος, eye of a needle, Matthieu 19:24 (WH, txt., τρῆμα).†
SYN.: τρῆμα, τρυμαλιά

G5170.def:
Τρύφαινα, -ης, ἡ 
Tryphæna: Romains 16:12 (see Lft., Phi., 175 f.; MM, xxv).†

G5171.def:
τρυφάω, -ῶ
(τρυφή), [in LXX: Néhémie 9:25 (עָדַן hithp.), Ésaïe 66:11 (עָנַג hithp.), Sir.14:4 * ;] 
to live daintily, luxuriously, to fare sumptuously: Jacques 5:5 (cf. ἐν-τρυφάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), στρηνιάω

G5172.def:
τρυφή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for עָדַן ;] 
softness, daintiness, luxuriousness: Luc 7:25, 2 Pierre 2:13.†

G5173.def:
Τρυφῶσα, -ης, ἡ, ς, ἡ 
Tryphosa: Romains 16:12 (see Lft., Phi., 175 f.).†

G5174.def:
Τρῳάς (Rec. Τρω-), -άδος, ἡ 
Troas, a city near the Hellespont: Actes 16:8, 11 20:5-6, 2 Corinthiens 2:12, 2 Timothée 4:13.†

G5175.def:
Τρωγύλλιον
(also written -γύλιον, -γίλιον, -ία, see Bl., § 6, 3), -ου 
Trogyllium, a city of Ionia: Actes 20:15 (WH, txt., R, txt., om.).†

G5176.def:
τρώγω 
__1. prop., of animals, to gnaw, munch, crunch (Hom., al.). 
__2. Of men, to eat raw food, as vegetables, nuts, etc. (Hdt., al.). 
__3. In late vernacular, simply to eat (= ἐσθίω): Matthieu 24:38, Jean 6:54, 56-58 13:18 (LXX ἐσθίων) (see Kennedy, Sources, 82, 155; MM, xxv).†

G5177.def:
τυγχάνω 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 19:5 (מָצָא), Job 3:21 7:2 17:1, Proverbes 30:23 (without definite Heb. equiv.), Wis.15:19, 1Ma.11:42, 3Ma.3:7, al. ;] 
__I. Trans. 
__1. to hit (opposite to ἁμαρτάνω, to miss the mark: Hom., Xen., al.). 
__2. to hit upon, light upon; 
__(a) of persons, to meet with, fall in with: absol., ptcp., ὁ τυχών, a chance person, anyone (Lat. quivis), οὐ τυχών, not common or ordinary, Actes 19:11 28:2; 
__(b) of things, to reach, get, obtain: with genitive of thing(s) Luc 20:35, Actes 24:3 26:22 27:3, 2 Timothée 2:10 Hébreux 8:6 11:35. 
__II. Intrans., to happen; of things, to happen, chance, befall: impers., εἰ τύχοι, it may be, perhaps, 1 Corinthiens 14:10 15:37; so ptcp., τυχόν (old accusative absol.; see M, Pr., 74), 1 Corinthiens 16:6 
(cf. ἐν-, ὑπερ-εν-, ἐπι-, παρα-, συν-τυγχάνω).† 
τυχόν, adv., see: τυγχάνω

G5178.def:
τυμπανίζω
(τύμπανον, a kettle-drum), [in LXX: 1 Rois 21:13 (14) (17 pi?) * ;] 
__1. to beat a drum. 
__2. to torture by beating, beat to death (cf. Westc. on He, l.with): pass., Hébreux 11:35.†

G5179.def:
τύπος, -ου, ὁ
(τύπτω), [in LXX: Exode 25:39 (40) (תַּבְנִית), Amos 5:26, 3Ma.3:30, 4Ma.6:19 * ;] 
__1. the mark of a blow: τῶν ἥλων, Jean 20:25. 
__2. An impression, impress, the stamp made by a die; hence, a figure, image: Actes 7:43 (LXX). 
__3. form (Plat.): Romains 6:17; the sense or substance of a letter (3Mac, l.with), Actes 23:25. 
__4. an example, pattern: Actes 7:44, Hébreux 8:6" (LXX) ; in ethical sense, Philippiens 3:17, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:7, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:9, 1 Timothée 4:12, Tite 2:7, 1 Pierre 5:3; in doctrinal sense, type (see ICC, in l), Romains 5:14.† 
τυπικῶς, adv. 
(τύπος), 
__(a) typically (Greg. Naz.) 
__(b) by way of example: 1 Corinthiens 10:11.†
SYN.: see: ὑποτύπωσις

G5180.def:
τύπτω 
[in LXX chiefly for hi. ;] 
to strike, smite, beat: with accusative, Matthieu 24:49, Marc 15:19, Luc 12:45, Actes 18:17 21:32 23:2-3; of mourners, τὰ στήθη, Luc 18:13 23:48; ἐπὶ τ. σιαγόνα, Luc 6:29; εἰς τ. κεφαλήν, Matthieu 27:30. Metaphorical, of God inflicting evil: Actes 23:3 (cf. Exode 8:2, Eze.7:9, al.); of disquieting conscience, 1 Corinthiens 8:12.†

G5181.def:
1. an absolute sovereign , unlimited by law or constitution, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: not applied to old hereditary sovereignties βασιλεῖαι); such as those of (Homer) or of Sparta; for the term rather regards the irregular way in which the power was gained , than the way in which it was exercised , being applied to the mild Pisistratus, but not to the despotic kings of Persia. However, the word soon came to imply reproach, like our tyrant , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. in a wider sense, the tyrant's son , or any member of his family , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;so, ἡ τύραννος was both the queen herself or a princess , (Euripides) 
3. τύραννος, ον, as adjective kingly, royal , [variant datesTragica Adespota 
4. imperious, despotic , (Thucydides); τύραννα δρᾶν (Sophocles Tragicus) 
τύραννος is probably from same Root as κύριος, κοίρανος. (ML)

G5184.def:
Τύρος, -ου, ἡ 
Tyre, a maritime city of Phænicia: Marc 7:31, Actes 21:3, 7; Τ. κ, Σιδών, Matthieu 11:21-22 15:21, Marc 3:8 7:24, Luc 6:17 10:13-14.†

G5185.def:
τυφλός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX for עִוֵּר ;] 
blind: as subst., ὁ τ., Matthieu 9:27, Marc 8:22, Luc 4:18" (LXX), Jean 5:3, al. Metaphorical: Matthieu 15:14 23:16-26, Jean 9:39-41, Romains 2:19, 2 Pierre 1:9, Apocalypse 3:17.

G5186.def:
τυφλόω, -ῶ
(τυφλός), [in LXX: Ésaïe 42:19 (עִוֵּר), Tob.7:7 א, Wis.2:21 א * ;] 
to blind, make blind: metaphorically, Jean 12:40 (LXX, καμμύω), 2 Corinthiens 4:4, 1 Jean 2:11.†

G5187.def:
τυφόω, -ῶ
(τῦφος, smoke; metaphorically, conceit), 
prop., to wrap in smoke; used only metaphorically, to puff up, becloud with pride: pass., 1 Timothée 3:6 6:4, 2 Timothée 3:4 (Dem., Arist., al.).†

G5188.def:
τύφω
(τῦφος, smoke), 
to raise a smoke; pass., to smoke: Matthieu 12:20 (LXX, καπνιζόμενον).†

G5189.def:
τυφωνικός, -ή, -όν
(τῦφων, a hurricane, typhoon) 
tempestuous: Actes 27:14.†

G5190.def:
τύχικος (T, Rec., Τυχικός), -ου, ὁ
Tychicus: Actes 20:4, Éphésiens 6:21, Colossiens 4:7, 2 Timothée 4:12, Tite 3:12.†

G5191.def:
ὑακίνθινος, -η, -ον
(ὑάκινθος), [in LXX for תַּחַשׁ, תְּכֵלֶת ;] 
of hyacinth, hyacinthine (see: ὑάκινθος), "doubtless meant to describe the blue smoke of a sulphurous flame" (Swete): Apocalypse 9:17 (Hom., Eur., al.).†

G5194.def:
ὕαλος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Job 28:17 (זְכוּכִית) * ;] 
__1. (Hdt.) a clear transparent stone. 
__2. (from Plat. on) glass: Apocalypse 21:18, 21.†

G5195.def:
ὑβρίζω
(ὕβρις), [in LXX for גֵּאֶה, etc. ;] 
__1. intrans., to wax wanton, run riot. 
__2. Trans., to outrage, insult, treat insolently: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 22:6, Luc 11:45 18:32, Actes 14:5, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:2.†

G5196.def:
ὕβρις, -εως, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 
__1. wantonness, insolence. 
__2. = ὕβρισμα, an act of wanton violence, an outrage, injury: 2 Corinthiens 12:10; metaphorically, of a loss by sea (find.), Actes 27:10, 21 (see MM, xxv).†

G5197.def:
ὑβριστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὑβρίζω), [in LXX chiefly for גֵּאֶה ;] 
a violent, insolent man: Romains 1:20, 1 Timothée 1:13 (EV, injurious).† 
SYN.: ἀλαζών, ὑπερήφανος, see Tr., Syn., § xxix

G5198.def:
ὑγιαίνω 
(ὑγιής), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלוֹם, and frequently in To ;] 
to be sound, healthy, in good health: Luc 5:31 7:10 15:27, 3Jo.2. In Past. Epp. (as also in cl.) metaphorically, ὑ. ἐν τ. πίστει, Tite 1:13 ; τ. πίστει, τ. ἀγάπῃ, τ. ὑπομονῇ, Tite 2:2; ἡ ὑγιαίνουσα διδασκαλία, 1 Timothée 1:10, 2 Timothée 4:3, Tite 1:9 2:1 ; λόγοι ὑγιαίνοντες, 1 Timothée 6:3, 2 Timothée 1:13.†

G5199.def:
ὑγιής, -ές, accusative, ὑγιῆ (Attic usually -ιᾶ), 
[in LXX for חַי, etc. ;] 
sound, whole, healthy: Matthieu 12:13 15:31, Jhn.5:[4], 6, 9, 11, 14, 15 7:23, Actes 4:10; before ἀπό, Marc 5:34; of words, opinions, etc. (as in cl.), metaphorically, λόγος, Tite 2:8.†
